decision: Deliver tenant-isolated table choros.mcp_tool (migration 040: 9 columns tenant_id,id,name,description,declares jsonb DEFAULT '[]',pure_compute boolean,resource_ops jsonb DEFAULT '[]',created_at,updated_at; PK(tenant_id,id); UNIQUE(tenant_id,name); FORCE RLS per T-0013; DB CHECK (declares <> '[]'::jsonb) OR (pure_compute = true); choros_app DML-only; idempotent dev seed of >=3 rows ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) plus one new pure module src/core/mcp-tool-registry.ts. The module re-uses (never re-declares) EffectDeclaration/classifyTool/verifyEffectGrants from ./effect-resource.js and Grant/ResourceType/Operation/isEffective from ./grant-lattice.js, and imports the same GrantSource type from ./grant-resolver.js. The agent toolset is a deterministic, side-effect-free async query over grants (resolveAgentToolset) — never a stored per-agent list: a tool is reachable iff EVERY resource_ops {resourceType,operation} pair is covered by an effective same-tenant grant (empty resource_ops + empty declares => reachable for any grant-holder; zero grants => empty toolset). resource_ops is a distinct typed axis from declares (object-model grants vs external-effect grants); both axes must be covered. pure_compute is derived at write-time by validateMcpToolWrite via classifyTool (caller-supplied value never trusted), malformed declares is rejected before persist with a typed error. The gateway invoke-path is NOT a new resolver edge: the EXISTING resolveFor op='invoke' seam (deps.effects + invokeCtx.declares + verifyEffectGrants) already enforces effect grants; the composition root passes mcp_tool.declares into the existing InvokeContext.declares. grant-resolver.ts is intentionally NOT edited (most proportionate reading of FR-10/C-4 since the additive seam already exists); the Postgres McpToolSource DAO and live migration apply defer to T-0053 (static-now ports). All 23 AC trace to 15 fitness functions.

rejected_alternatives.option: Add mcpTools?: McpToolSource optional field on ResolverDeps and read the registry inside resolveFor
rejected_alternatives.why_not: The invoke-path effect seam already exists (invokeCtx.declares + deps.effects); reading the registry inside the PDP couples authority to the tool catalog, creates a second handle->data edge, and risks single-resolver.sh / AC-16 for zero benefit. Registry read belongs at the composition root that already wires deps.effects.

rejected_alternatives.option: Match the toolset from declares alone, dropping the resource_ops column
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Forces semantic interpretation of free-text effect claims to infer object-model access, re-introducing the free-text dependency the model structurally forbids (CONCEPT.md sec3, hypothesis sec1). resource_ops is the typed grant-matching surface.

rejected_alternatives.option: Store the resolved toolset as a per-agent tool list / cache
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Violates NF-6/AC-12/AC-23: breaks '0 roles -> 0 tools' liveness, a revocation would need a toolset migration, and it is not TOCTOU-safe. The query is cheap and the only source of the agent's tool list.
GrantSource.getGrants returns Promise<Grant[]> (T-0021); a sync wrapper would fork the shared port. The function is async with two awaited port reads then a pure fold.

rejected_alternatives.option: DB trigger / PL-pgSQL re-implementation of full pure_compute consistency for non-empty declares
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Duplicates the closed EffectKind authority axis into the DB. The DB CHECK covers only the mechanical empty-array floor (FR-5); the TS write path (validateMcpToolWrite via classifyTool) owns the non-empty case; fitness FF-2/FF-3 guard both.

fields.name: tenant_id
fields.type: uuid NOT NULL (leading PK component, T-0013 RLS key, no default)

fields.name: description
fields.type: text NULL (never in an access decision)

fields.name: pure_compute
fields.type: boolean NOT NULL (= classifyTool(declares).pure, stored at write-time)

object_model.entity: McpToolSource (TS injected port — registry read; in-memory static-now, Postgres RLS DAO in T-0053; NOT a ResolverDeps field)

fields.name: employeeId
fields.type: string (agent employee.id, kind='agent'; abstract — no agent_card dependency)

object_model.entity: McpToolWriteResult (TS discriminated union — write-path guard output)

fields.name: ok:true variant
fields.type: { ok: true; declares: EffectDeclaration[]; pureCompute: boolean }

fields.name: signature
fields.type: (tool: McpToolRow, grants: readonly Grant[], tenantId: string, nowMs: number) => boolean

object_model.entity: resolveAgentToolset (TS async query — the toolset = query over grants)

fields.name: signature
fields.type: (input: ResolveToolsetInput, deps: { grants: GrantSource; tools: McpToolSource }) => Promise<McpToolRow[]>

contracts: C-1 T-0040: reads mcp_tool.declares (jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]') and parses via classifyTool from T-0034 to derive external_invoke criticality. Column type and semantics frozen by this ADR.
C-2 T-0042: may call resolveAgentToolset(input, {grants, tools}) to display the post-hire toolset. Signature, ResolveToolsetInput shape, and McpToolSource port shape are frozen.
C-3 Stage-2 agent runtime: consumes resolveAgentToolset to populate the live MCP server list before each Agent Task; same frozen signatures and port shapes.

C-4 T-0021 resolveFor invoke-path: NOT edited. The composition root passes mcp_tool.declares into the EXISTING InvokeContext.declares of resolveFor(deps, handle, subject, 'invoke', invokeCtx); deps.effects + verifyEffectGrants enforce effect grants. No new ResolverDeps field, no second resolver edge.

Frozen public surfaces (NF-2/AC-15): no export in grant-lattice.ts, object-handle.ts, effect-resource.ts, types.ts is renamed/removed/re-signed; grant-resolver.ts is byte-unchanged. ci/checks/single-resolver.sh stays green (AC-16).

Import contract (AC-17): src/core/mcp-tool-registry.ts imports EffectDeclaration, classifyTool, verifyEffectGrants from ./effect-resource.js and Grant, ResourceType, Operation, isEffective from ./grant-lattice.js and the GrantSource type from ./grant-resolver.js — re-declaring none.
ci/checks/known_tenant_tables.txt gains the single line 'mcp_tool' in alphabetical position; the existing cross-tenant CI probe passes with zero test-source change (AC-5, NF-7).
Migration seam: T-0043 owns 040 (and 041 if needed); 032-039 are occupied/reserved by in-flight parallel tasks and MUST NOT be used.

fitness_functions.rule: Migration 040 declares CREATE TABLE choros.mcp_tool with PK(tenant_id,id), UNIQUE(tenant_id,name), and all 9 FR-1 columns with correct types (AC-1).
fitness_functions.ci_check: grep -E 'CREATE TABLE +choros\.mcp_tool' migrations/040_mcp_tool.sql && assert PK (tenant_id, id), UNIQUE (tenant_id, name), and the 9 columns/types are present

fitness_functions.rule: DB CHECK enforces pure_compute=true when declares is empty: declares='[]' with pure_compute=false is rejected (AC-7).
fitness_functions.ci_check: grep -E "declares <> '\[\]'::jsonb\) OR \(pure_compute = true" migrations/040_mcp_tool.sql ; DB test inserting declares='[]',pure_compute=false raises a CHECK violation

fitness_functions.rule: validateMcpToolWrite derives pure_compute = classifyTool(declares).pure (false for any valid non-empty declares, true for []); caller-supplied pure_compute never trusted (AC-8).
fitness_functions.ci_check: unit test asserting validateMcpToolWrite(rawDeclares).pureCompute === classifyTool(rawDeclares).pure across empty and non-empty cases

fitness_functions.rule: Malformed declares (invalid JSON shape, unknown kind, non-array) is rejected before persist with a typed error (AC-9).
fitness_functions.ci_check: unit test asserting validateMcpToolWrite on each malformed shape returns { ok:false, error:'malformed_declares' } and no row is persisted

fitness_functions.rule: resolveAgentToolset returns exactly the tools whose full resource_ops set is covered by effective grants: full-coverage inclusion, grant add/revoke flips membership, zero-role->empty, partial coverage excludes, empty resource_ops+empty declares reachable for any grant-holder (AC-10/11/12/21/22).
fitness_functions.ci_check: unit tests on resolveAgentToolset and isToolReachable covering AC-10, AC-11, AC-12, AC-21, AC-22

fitness_functions.rule: resolveAgentToolset is deterministic: two identical calls return deep-equal results (AC-13, NF-4).
fitness_functions.ci_check: unit test asserting deepEqual of two resolveAgentToolset calls with identical grants snapshot, tools, and nowMs

fitness_functions.rule: mcp_tool is fully tenant-isolated: listed in known_tenant_tables.txt (alphabetical), FORCE RLS + USING(tenant_id=current_setting) policy + choros_app DML-only present in 040, and the existing cross-tenant probe passes with no test-source change (AC-2/AC-3/AC-4/AC-5/AC-19).
fitness_functions.ci_check: grep -x 'mcp_tool' ci/checks/known_tenant_tables.txt ; grep 'FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY' and the isolation policy and 'GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ... TO choros_app' in migrations/040_mcp_tool.sql ; run existing cross-tenant RLS test unmodified

fitness_functions.rule: src/core/mcp-tool-registry.ts is a pure module: no pg/fs/net/http/node built-in IO import (NF-1, AC-14).
src/core/mcp-tool-registry.ts re-declares none of EffectKind/EffectDeclaration/ResourceType/Operation; it imports them from ./effect-resource.js and ./grant-lattice.js (AC-17).
fitness_functions.ci_check: grep -nE 'type EffectKind\b|interface EffectDeclaration\b|type ResourceType\b|type Operation\b' src/core/mcp-tool-registry.ts returns nothing; the imports are present

fitness_functions.rule: Frozen public surfaces unchanged: grant-lattice.ts, object-handle.ts, effect-resource.ts, types.ts byte-frozen; grant-resolver.ts byte-unchanged (AC-15, NF-2).
fitness_functions.ci_check: git diff --exit-code <base> -- src/core/grant-lattice.ts src/core/object-handle.ts src/core/effect-resource.ts src/core/types.ts src/core/grant-resolver.ts

fitness_functions.rule: No table or column stores a per-agent tool list (AC-23, NF-6).
Migration 040 dev seed has >=3 rows ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING covering one integration_endpoint, one messaging_channel, and one pure-compute (declares='[]') tool (AC-6).
fitness_functions.ci_check: assert migrations/040_mcp_tool.sql seed block inserts >=3 mcp_tool rows with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING and the three required declares shapes
